title: Greek Poetry - Meter and Scansion
objectives: Connect meter to meaning in Homer

grammar.explanation: Greek poetry is quantitative, based on syllable length rather than stress. The dactylic hexameter, used in Homer and Hesiod, consists of six feet, each a dactyl (— ∪ ∪) or spondee (— —), with the fifth foot usually dactylic and sixth always spondaic.

paradigms.name: Dactylic Hexameter Structure
content: Caesura: penthemimeral (after 5th half-foot) or bucolic diaeresis (after 4th foot)

paradigms.name: Metrical Phenomena
rows: Final short vowel drops before initial vowel
Long vowel shortened before another vowel

readingPassage.analysis: DAC | DAC | SPOND | SPOND | DAC | SPOND. Penthemimeral caesura after θεά. The heavy spondees give weight to the opening. Πηληϊάδεω shows synizesis.
